title: FaultDx governed data package manifest contract
description: Defines one common package envelope without merging the TPDX, DEKG, and FHKB record contracts or route semantics.

TPDX.note: Schema 4.2 is the selected TPDX working baseline. Schema 4.1 is a rollback/comparison baseline, not an alternative package contract.

identity_rules.canonical_json: UTF-8 RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme with no insignificant whitespace.

package_id.encoding: Canonical JSON array in the listed order.

content_digest.input: The complete package manifest after package_id is set, excluding only the top-level content_digest field.

artifact_id.rule: ART_ plus SHA-256 of the canonical JSON array [artifact_role, relative_path].
artifact_id.collision_behavior: Reject the package when one artifact_id names different role/path content or a path is repeated under another artifact_id.

identity_rules.duplicate_package_behavior: Byte-equivalent canonical manifests with the same package_id and content_digest are idempotent. The same package_id with a different content_digest is an identity collision and fails closed.

path_rules.symlink_rule: A production validator resolves the target without following it outside the package root and rejects an escaping symlink.

artifact_rules.required_integrity: Every artifact is verified against its declared byte_size and SHA-256 before record-contract validation.
artifact_rules.record_count: record_count is required for record_payload, exclusions, and review_queue artifacts; it is null for artifacts without records.
artifact_rules.record_payload_count: Component and DEKG/FHKB packages contain exactly one record_payload artifact. A tpdx_release contains no record_payload artifact.
artifact_rules.unknown_media_type: Reject unless a later reviewed contract version allowlists it.

masking_rules.package_integrity_digest: SHA-256 over the immutable masking manifest bytes; historical hashes inside that manifest remain unchanged source metadata.
masking_rules.coverage: Every artifact with requires_masking=true is named by exactly one effective masking reference. Every covered_artifact_id must resolve to an artifact in the same package. Overlapping effective coverage is rejected as ambiguous.
masking_rules.multiple_runs: A package may reference multiple masking runs when their effective covered artifact sets are disjoint.
masking_rules.partial_runs: One masking reference may cover only part of the package, but total effective coverage must cover every artifact that requires masking.
masking_rules.state_separation: Masking success never sets serving_safe, route_eligible, review_status, promotion_status, package_status, or release status.

component_rules.tpdx_release_only: Only tpdx_release packages may contain component_refs.
component_rules.acceptance: Every referenced component must be accepted, match its referenced manifest digest, use Schema 4.2, and belong to the same release_id.
component_rules.component_type_cardinality: A tpdx_release may reference zero or one accepted package of each allowed component type. Two references with the same package_type are rejected even when their package IDs differ.
component_rules.future_partitioning: Supporting multiple packages of one component type requires a later contract version with an explicit partition identity, non-overlap rules, and deterministic composition order.
component_rules.dependency_behavior: Reject missing, conflicting, self-referential, circular, incompatible, unaccepted, or duplicate component references.

released_requirements: all required masking evidence is verified
all artifacts and record payloads validate
all TPDX component references are accepted

route_boundaries.TPDX: promotion_status may be candidate or reviewed; a released package requires reviewed.
route_boundaries.DEKG: promotion_status is not_applicable and content remains evidence_only.
route_boundaries.FHKB: promotion_status is not_applicable and content remains candidate.

decision_rules.failure: Validation failure never downgrades, promotes, accepts, or releases a package automatically.

validation_order: Recompute package_id from the governed identity tuple.
Resolve every package-relative path inside the package root and reject collisions or escapes.
Verify the lineage source manifest exists and matches lineage.source_manifest_digest.
Verify artifact existence, byte_size, and SHA-256.
Verify masking-manifest existence, SHA-256, run_id, review state, and exact effective artifact coverage.
Validate the record_payload with the selected route-specific record contract.
For DEKG and FHKB, require the route payload release, source, lineage, masking, and serving fields to agree with the common envelope mappings.
Resolve TPDX component references, verify identity/digest/status/release compatibility, and detect cycles.
Validate decision-state prerequisites and route promotion boundaries.
Recompute content_digest and check duplicate package identity behavior.

DEKG.binding_rule: The wrapped dekg_evidence_v2 payload must exactly match release_id, source_id, source_version, manifest_digest/lineage source digest, lineage_ref, and serving_safe. Its masking_status must be compatible with the effective masking evidence covering the record payload.

FHKB.binding_rule: The wrapped fhkb_case_v1 payload must exactly match release_id, source_id, source_version, manifest_digest/lineage source digest, lineage_ref, and serving_safe. Its masking_status must be compatible with the effective masking evidence covering the record payload.

TPDX.mapping: Each component record_payload validates directly against the self-contained Schema 4.2 contract; the release package references accepted component manifests without copying records.

migration.phase_1: Producers continue emitting their existing route-specific packages; the common envelope is optional and offline.
migration.phase_2: Reviewed adapters wrap one existing package at a time and preserve the original record payload and manifest evidence.
migration.phase_3: After consumer and independent review, package validators may require the common envelope at controlled boundaries.

rollback.action: Remove the optional common-envelope binding and resume direct use of the unchanged route-specific contract and masking manifest.
rollback.schema_4_1: Retained only as the governed TPDX comparison/rollback baseline; rollback activation is a separate decision.

affected_consumers: DEKG evidence producer and index preparation
FHKB case producer and index preparation

implementation_handoff.prerequisite: The FROZEN v1 contract is the approved envelope boundary. Production implementation requires a separately allocated pipeline/KG task with an explicit write set and all recorded implementation conditions.
implementation_handoff.future_scope: Shared loader/validator, producer adapters, filesystem digest verification, dependency resolution, and governed real-package validation.
implementation_handoff.excluded_now: No producer, runtime, graph, index, Data RC, or real-data change is authorized by this contract-design task.
